q: Which statement defines a joint (articulation)?
options: Any place where a bone meets another bone, a cartilage or a tooth
A place where two bones move freely against each other
A cord of dense connective tissue that joins two bones
The smooth cartilage that covers the end of a bone

q: Name the pinned joint.

Middle: the two forearm bones side by side, joined along their length by a broad sheet of fibers. Right: a tooth cut lengthwise, sitting in its bony socket, with a thin layer of fibers between the root and the socket.

q: What feature separates a synovial joint from fibrous and cartilaginous joints?
options: It occurs in the limbs but not in the head
Its bones are joined by fibrocartilage
A fluid-filled space separates the bone ends
Its bone ends are covered by a layer of periosteum

Fibrous joints include immobile and slightly movable ones

Wide bands of fibrous tissue lie between the bones
The skull bones are joined by fibrocartilage

q: Why does a syndesmosis usually allow more movement than a suture?

It has a narrow fluid-filled space between its two bones
Its fibers are longer and the bones farther apart

q: A patient keeps an injured knee completely still in a brace for many weeks. Why can this harm the knee's articular cartilage?

Without loading and release, less fluid is pumped through the cartilage

A view from above the shin bone shows the two C-shaped pads and where the crossing ligaments attach. A front view shows the kneecap in the tendon from the thigh, the ligament below it, and a ligament on each side of the knee.

q: Name the pinned rim of fibrocartilage.

Two tendons pass near the joint, one running over the top and one running down the front of the arm in its own sheath.
